races.name: Queen Anne Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Cicero's Gift
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' six-year-old showed good form winning at Goodwood in Similar conditions, but this race has too many prominent horses vying for position and he is likely to find himself further back than his front-running instincts demand, blunting his effectiveness.|
runners_data.comment: Cicero's Gift has won twice in its last five starts and acts on soft, good and AW, but the ground here may be on the quick side for this one, and last time out's seventh in the Lockinge — beaten over seven lengths — tempers enthusiasm despite that Group 1 backdrop.

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old has three wins at 9-10f and drops back to a mile here, arriving 31 days fresh with James Doyle aboard — his natural desire to race prominently means the rear position he's been assigned in this crowded pace picture is particularly artificial and his chance hinges on a truly slow early pace.|
runners_data.comment: Damysus arrives on the back of a 6¼-length thumping in a Group 1 at Newbury last time, with lack of pace exposed over a mile, and today's test looks similarly sharp for a horse who really comes into his own at nine or ten furlongs.

runners_data.name: Docklands
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's six-year-old bounced back with a win at Sandown last time (51 days ago) and wears a hood, suggesting he can be keen — a horse who wants to race up with the pace but the sheer volume of similar types means he'll likely be squeezed into a role that doesn't suit, weakening his prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Docklands won this race last year and shaped with promise on return when a close third in a Group 1 at Sha Tin 51 days ago, so course-and-distance form reads well; first-time headgear and a trainer in form add appeal, though a rating of 118 versus our figure of 114 suggests the handicapper holds a slight edge.

runners_data.name: First Conquest
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Charlie Appleby on this consistent performer who has placed in his last five starts, but 179 days off the track is a significant fitness query and, though he wants to race prominently, he faces the same positional squeeze as several rivals in this pace-heavy field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and absent for 179 days, First Conquest shaped respectably with a close third in a Meydan Group 2 last time but looks likely to fill a pacemaking role for better-fancied stablemates here, making it very hard to fancy at big odds.

runners_data.name: More Thunder
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old won at Newbury last month and has strong form at seven furlongs on Good ground, making this step back up to a mile for Tom Marquand a mild query — but he is one of the few prominent types who can realistically hold a genuine position just behind Opera Ballo, which is a key tactical advantage in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ran a career-best when runner-up in the Lockinge Group 1 last time, showing real progression at a mile on a sound surface, and this stiff track could bring him even closer to the principals — though there's a nagging question over whether that ceiling has now been reached.

runners_data.name: Notable Speech
runners_data.note: William Buick and Charlie Appleby combine on the joint top-rated runner, who has three wins on Firm ground and a win at this exact trip and course profile — his ability to travel prominently without being in the overcrowded scrimmage makes him a natural fit for the race shape that is most likely to unfold.|
runners_data.comment: Notable Speech has won five G1s and was imperious when scooting clear in the Lockinge last time, marking it out as probably the world's number-one miler; carrying 128 lb from stall 1, the course record is a minor query but fast ground suits and this is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Opera Ballo
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Opera Ballo has won five of his nine starts with four coming on Good to Firm ground, and Loughnane can exploit the absence of any genuine pace rival to control the contest — headgear noted (hood), which helps him travel kindly, and 53 days since his last run is a minor query but he arrives in form.|
runners_data.comment: Four wins in its last five starts, Opera Ballo has progressed into one of Europe's leading milers — most recently dictating and winning the bet365 Mile (Group 2) at Sandown by 3l from a multiple G1 winner — and acts on today's conditions. First-time headgear is the one unknown.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old arrives just 10 days after his last run and recorded his most recent win on Soft ground at seven furlongs — the step up to a mile on Good to Firm and the compressed turnaround are both queries, and like several others here he is a natural front-runner who will struggle to express that in this particular field.|
runners_data.comment: Ten Bob Tony won a Group 3 at Epsom ten days ago, but that victory came on ground with cut and this looks a stiffer test — rated 108 on our figures and ranked last of nine, there are serious doubts about whether it can match those elite rivals here.

runners_data.name: Zeus Olympios
runners_data.note: K R Burke's four-year-old has won three of his five starts at eight furlongs on Good ground and arrives in solid form despite back-to-back thirds — Clifford Lee takes the ride and he is one of the few runners whose form profile genuinely suits the trip, surface and pace shape, making him a logical threat if the main protagonists are at all vulnerable.|
runners_data.comment: Zeus Olympios arrives on the back of a career-best effort when finishing third in the Lockinge Stakes, and his three wins in his last five starts underline a horse in fine fettle — the main reservation is whether he can quite bridge the gap to outright Group 1 winning class today.

races.paceDynamic: Opera Ballo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him early, Billy Loughnane can control tempo from the outset on the straight Ascot mile on Good to Firm ground. The field is unusually stacked with prominent-running types — Cicero's Gift, Docklands, First Conquest, Ten Bob Tony and More Thunder all want to race prominently, but they cannot all occupy those positions, meaning several will be shuffled into a midfield they don't naturally inhabit. Opera Ballo therefore faces a genuinely uncrowded lead, able to dictate a measured gallop before quickening from the front in the home straight, a setup that on fast ground at Ascot historically rewards the horse controlling the race. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses who can hold a clean position just behind the leader and quicken in a straight line — pure prominent-to-front runners, particularly those with proven Good to Firm form over this course and distance. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically secure that position; of the overcrowded group, More Thunder and Notable Speech are best placed to win the battle for the seats directly behind Opera Ballo, with the redistributed runners — Cicero's Gift, Docklands, First Conquest and Ten Bob Tony — likely to find themselves further back than ideal.

watchPoints.text: Opera Ballo sets the pace entirely alone — watch whether Loughnane elects to use that freedom to slow the race to a crawl, which would compress the field and bring more horses into play in a sprint finish.

More Thunder and Notable Speech will both try to sit directly behind Opera Ballo; if they clash for that position in the first two furlongs, it could create early crowding that disrupts the rhythm of those behind them.

First Conquest returns after 179 days off the track — watch the betting market closely for any drift that signals connections are treating this as a comeback run rather than a serious Group 1 attempt.

The Good to Firm going (confirmed across all races at Ascot today) is consistent and fast — horses with Soft or Heavy form only should be watched for any signs of being unsuited once they hit the faster ground in the home straight.

Ten Bob Tony races just 10 days after his last outing at seven furlongs; watch his early behaviour to see whether Shoemark tries to push forward aggressively from the start or accepts a midfield berth, as either choice affects the pace map around Opera Ballo.

races.name: Coventry Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay Of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Three wins from three starts including two over five furlongs at Goodwood on Good, Hugo Palmer filly stepping up to six furlongs; her natural front-running speed means she'll want to be close to the pace but the congestion of prominent types in a 22-runner field is likely to see her race further back than she'd ideally like.
runners_data.comment: Rattled off back-to-back wins before a game half-length second in Listed company latest, and acts on today's going and distance, making this high-class colt a genuine threat — the main concern is whether he's now near his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Bull Shark
runners_data.note: David Egan partner has four runs in the book with no wins, consistently placing third or worse, and his two most recent efforts over six furlongs on Good ground both resulted in thirds; a style profile that defies easy categorisation makes him difficult to place tactically.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but not without appeal — Bull Shark quickened clear latest at The Curragh only to be caught late, suggesting timing rather than ability was the issue. A very useful sprint prospect who acts on varying ground, though ranked 18th on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: One run, one second over six furlongs on Good at Newmarket for Brian Meehan; a natural front-runner by instinct who will find the sheer number of pace-committed rivals in this field will push him wider and deeper than he wants to be during the crucial early stages.
runners_data.comment: Cilician shaped with distinct promise on debut, going down by just half a length at Nottingham over today's trip, and speed in the pedigree suggests the six furlongs suits; however, winless in recent starts and carrying 129lb from stall 9, there's still plenty to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore aboard this Aidan O'Brien runner who won over six furlongs on Good and placed over five on Heavy; comes here on a 38-day break and though his front-running tendency is natural, the volume of pace rivals in this field means he is likely to find himself operating from a more restrained position than suits.
runners_data.comment: Confucius took a Naas maiden by four lengths last time, that form already looking solid, and he gets the nod from the top course jockey in a yard that won this 12 months ago; open to further progress and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Cut A Dash
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's Sean Levey-ridden debutant winner over five furlongs on Good; clearly a horse with an engine but with only one run and a desire to race prominently, the 22-runner field makes it highly unlikely he secures the forward berth his style craves.
runners_data.comment: Won on debut at York with plenty in hand, quickening clear cosily by three lengths on good ground over today's trip, and that novice form looks strong enough to merit this step up in class — the sole risk is how she handles 34 days off and the rise in grade.

runners_data.name: Easy Answer
runners_data.note: Michael Bell runner with a single third-place effort over six furlongs on Good to his name and the lightly raced flag applies; with a style profile that is genuinely uncertain, Cristian Demuro will need to play this race on feel, making tactical planning speculative.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of promise on debut at Yarmouth, finishing third — best of those held up — beaten just 1¼ lengths, and should improve stepping forward from that initial experience if ridden more positively over today's trip, though winless in recent starts remains the caveat.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: The Hamad Al Jehani stable runner placed second on his sole start over six furlongs on Good wearing headgear; a midfield-inclined type who is shown towards the rear of the field map as a natural consequence of the field shape, which broadly fits his likely race position.
runners_data.comment: Promising debut second at Lingfield, beaten 3l while finishing well after being outpaced, suggests ability — first-time headgear adds interest — but stepping up in class leaves Final Objective looking vulnerable despite that speed pedigree over today's trip.

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: William Buick teams up with James Ferguson's once-raced winner who scored over six furlongs at Newmarket on Good; his front-running instincts are genuine but with so many pace horses in this field he is effectively a prominent racer operating in a midfield slot, limiting his chance in a shape that requires positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Scored on debut at Newbury, quickening well to win by 1¼l, but that maiden form reads nothing special and our figures rank it well below most here — further progress needed to compete at this level.

runners_data.name: Great Barrier Reef
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's Wayne Lordan-partnered colt has won both his starts, both over six furlongs including on Good going, and he is one of the better-credentialed horses to actually secure a prominent pitch behind The Scallionator; his profile sits squarely in the scenario-A beneficiary bracket.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a Curragh Group 3 success last time, where he had a bit in hand and looked like 7f is well within compass — stiff track, sound surface and proven distance all in his favour, with the yard having won this last year. The main risk is handling a large field from stall 3.

runners_data.name: High King
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained colt ridden by Gavin Ryan, won on Good ground over six furlongs last time having been well beaten on debut; the bounce-back form is encouraging and he looks one of those likely to get a genuine hold on the prominent positions in this large field.
runners_data.comment: Franked a taking Fairyhouse win with an excellent turn of foot, and that 3½-length success reads well stepping up in class; the unplaced run on the other side of that coin and a stiff 129lb are the checks on enthusiasm here.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's Rossa Ryan mount has three starts over five furlongs, placing second twice and third once, all on Good ground; a hold-up type shown at the rear of the field map, which genuinely reflects his style, though the controlled pace in this race shape may not provide the strong finish he needs to arrive late.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless in recent starts, Jaan Ki Tukri has placed in all three latest outings and acts on today's going and distance — though stepping up in class looks the key test from stall 22 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Kamaal
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides this Jack Jones-trained runner who was fifth on debut over six furlongs on Good; the lightly raced flag and a profile showing no placings from one run makes this one of the more speculative entries, with no tactical angle available from the data.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and beaten three lengths on a modest Newbury maiden debut 32 days ago, Kamaal looks out of depth stepping up in class here, though today's trip and going hold no fears — a big ask at the foot of the weights.

runners_data.name: Mrair
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for George Scott on a colt who won over six furlongs at Windsor on Good and placed second at Newmarket on the same ground; consistent form over the trip and going, and he looks capable of securing a prominent position and running a strong race in the lead scenario.
runners_data.comment: Won a Lingfield novice by 3l on latest but that came in weaker company, and greenness remains a concern under 129lb from stall 14; with a trainer in form and more improvement likely as experience grows, the upside is real if inexperience doesn't cost.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's Charles Bishop-ridden filly has won both her starts, the more recent of which came over six furlongs on Good; consecutive wins and a genuine front-running tendency make her one of the horses most likely to actually occupy a position close behind The Scallionator, boosting her scenario-A prospects.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, including a smooth Goodwood success last time, give Night In Vegas solid claims, and the step up in class looks the obvious next test; acts on good and effective at today's trip, though 129 lb from stall 21 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Royal Heritage
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's James Doyle partnership won on debut over six furlongs on Soft only six days ago, which is a notably short turnaround for a juvenile; Doyle's booking adds interest but the quick reappearance is worth monitoring as a fitness and freshness factor.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a comfortable 3-length debut win at Hamilton six days ago and acts on good to soft over this trip, but the quick turnaround and a provisional rating of 102 ranked 15th of 22 suggest there are open questions — an improver worth noting, albeit untested beyond that promising maiden.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: James McDonald partners this K R Burke runner who won over five furlongs on Good on debut 27 days ago; stepping up to six furlongs on similar ground, he is a hold-up type shown towards the rear and is one of the more credible beneficiaries if the scenario-C late-closer shape emerges, though his form base is slender.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up on debut at Ayr and that form has been franked, marking this one out as potentially very useful stepping up in class; acts on the going and trip, though the hefty 129lb and draw 17 are factors to weigh against a short sample of evidence.

runners_data.name: Siouxperb
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's Hector Crouch-ridden colt won over six furlongs on Good at Ascot on debut and has been off the track for 56 days since; the course form is relevant and if he retains his condition after the break he should be competitive, with a prominent style that could see him grab a useful position.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up by four lengths on debut at Yarmouth, quickening clear with plenty in hand, and stays today's trip on this ground — a smart prospect returning off a short break, though 129 lb and 56 days off give rivals something to aim at.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's Kieran Shoemark-ridden runner won at Newmarket over six furlongs on Good last time, bouncing back from a debut unplaced effort; consistent improvement and a prominent style should allow Shoemark to find a decent position in the early stages.
runners_data.comment: Followed up debut experience with a narrow novice win at Nottingham 13 days ago, but this represents a sharp step up in grade and, ranked 16th of 22 on our figures, considerably more improvement will be needed to make an impact here.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this M D O'Callaghan runner who won on debut over six furlongs on Soft just nine days ago; a very quick turnaround for a two-year-old and the Soft ground form needs translating to Good to Firm conditions, making this an unknown quantity on going grounds.
runners_data.comment: Scraped home by a nose on debut at Goodwood nine days ago, with the form nothing special and the win flattered by a pace collapse — hard to fancy at the foot of the weights on these figures, though the scope to progress with that run under its belt offers the only realistic hook.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: The confirmed race leader for Michael Mulvany and Wesley Joyce, he won over six furlongs on Good last time and has been prominent in all three starts; the lone front-runner in a 22-runner field who can dictate his own fractions is a powerful tactical weapon on fast ground, and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers his chance only in scenarios where he is outrun, not where he dictates.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listowel maiden by three lengths 16 days ago and is clearly progressing, though carrying 129lb from stall 16 is a notable ask stepping into stronger company; breeding points to 6f/7f on good ground as the sweet spot, so conditions at least play to strengths.

runners_data.name: Treasurer
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' Rowan Scott-ridden runner was fourth on debut over six furlongs at Newmarket on Good 16 days ago; with no win or placing from one start and a genuinely uncertain style profile, there is limited tactical evidence to assess his likely position or chance.
runners_data.comment: Promising 3l fourth on debut at Nottingham shows ability, and today's trip and conditions suit, but ranked 19th of 22 on our figures, Treasurer has plenty to find in this company despite likely improvement still to come.

runners_data.name: Arizona Raider
runners_data.note: The second Michael Mulvany runner, ridden by W J Lee, has progressed from fifth over five furlongs on Soft to a win over eight furlongs on Good most recently; the step back to six furlongs is a question and as a natural prominent racer he is one of those who will likely be displaced into a midfield role by the sheer weight of pace in this field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Roscommon auction race last time on the step up in trip and drop in class, but ranks near the foot of the weights here and looks vulnerable at this level, with sounder ground at least suiting his action.

races.paceDynamic: The Scallionator is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and with just one horse likely to lead in a 22-runner field, the pace is set to be controlled and sustainable rather than truly searching. Wesley Joyce will dictate from the front and, with no meaningful challenger willing or able to push him, the fractions are likely to be honest but not punishing — a classic Group 2 juvenile setup where the leader can bowl along without burning fuel unnecessarily. This race shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently behind the leader and quicken cleanly off the steady tempo, rather than those making up ground from the rear. The field contains significantly more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate in their natural positions — Great Barrier Reef, High King, Mrair, Night In Vegas and Siouxperb are most likely to actually secure those coveted spots just off The Scallionator, while God Given Talent, Confucius, Cut A Dash, Adaay Of Scarlett, Cilician and Arizona Raider have enough pace to want to be prominent but will be squeezed back into midfield in this large field. In a race where the front-runner sets a controlled gallop and prominent racers dominate the frame, the clear tactical verdict is that horses drawn well and able to race in the first three or four positions behind the leader hold a decisive advantage over hold-up types, who will find the pace insufficient to generate the finish they need.

watchPoints.text: Great Barrier Reef and Night In Vegas are the two prominent horses most likely to actually secure positions close behind The Scallionator — watch both at the off to see if they get the jump on the field, as that would trigger scenario A decisively.

The Scallionator's uncontested lead is the foundation of the entire race shape — if any of the prominent types break sharply and push him for the lead early, the pace dynamic shifts materially and scenario B collapses.

Royal Heritage runs just six days after her debut win, an unusually short turnaround for a two-year-old; watch the pre-race paddock closely for any signs of freshness or fatigue that could undermine what looks like a strong booking for James Doyle.

The Harv and The Harv's Soft-ground form needs translating to Good to Firm — along with Night In Vegas and Royal Heritage, these horses won on Soft or Yielding conditions and the faster ground here is a legitimate query worth monitoring in the early market moves.

races.name: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Ain't Nobody
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up filly has shown smart form at 5f on good ground but her recent record shows she tends to be finishing late in modest positions; needs everything to go right from the back of a 26-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and again disappointing at York last time, Ain't Nobody is very erratic and not always resolute, though first-time headgear may sharpen focus, and it does hold course-and-distance form on today's ground.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's consistent six-year-old is a genuine 5f performer on good ground with three wins at the trip, races prominently by nature, and Paul Mulrennan's experience in big-field sprints is an asset; well-placed to get a good position.
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year and arrives in decent nick after finishing second in a Group 2 on latest start, so course-and-distance form stacks up well; the 133 lb burden from stall 18 is the obvious query, though a progressive return to form suggests fitness is no concern.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose natural style gives him undisputed lead — Michael Appleby's four-year-old will control the tempo from flag to finish; the key question is whether he can sustain his speed over 5f at this level.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time out, that run probably needed after 34 days off, Big Mojo is well-suited by today's 6f on fast ground and holds strong claims off 117 — the risk is getting caught too far back again as last year here showed.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: James McDonald takes the ride on this Simon & Ed Crisford horse who has won twice over 5f on good ground and was last seen placing in a competitive 6f contest; 80 days off the track is the only mild flag but he's a natural prominent type in good hands.
runners_data.comment: Held every chance on form credentials — acts on any going over 5f — but well held in a Group 1 last time and ranks 22nd of 26 on our figures; the first-time headgear and 80-day break add further uncertainty for a horse that simply may not be up to this level.

runners_data.name: Getreadytorumble
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for Jack Channon who has three wins at 5f, though on softer ground; a naturally prominent runner who is likely to find himself shuffled back in this enormous field and will need to work harder than his rating would suggest.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 2 last time — fair enough form — and Listed-placed with good prior profile, but ranked 21 of 26 on our figures and needs more improvement again to trouble these; the wide draw in a large field adds no help.

runners_data.name: Jakajaro
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's speedball won back-to-back 5f races on good ground and is a true prominent racer by inclination; Jamie Spencer will try to secure a position near the pace but the volume of front-runners makes this far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Shaped well when fourth in a Group 2 last time, going down by just 1¼ lengths only near the finish, and two wins in its last five starts show the progressive profile — yet stepping into this grade still leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Jm Jungle
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on soft for John & Sean Quinn but his good-ground record is patchy; his natural desire to be up with the pace will be tested in a 26-runner field and Jason Hart will struggle to position him ideally.
runners_data.comment: Shock Group 2 winner last year, but JM Jungle has failed to recapture that form this season, beaten seven lengths in a Group 2 last time — hard to fancy at these weights from stall 14, even if the trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Night Raider
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's five-year-old won back-to-back 5f races on soft and good and races prominently; James Doyle's big-field experience is relevant here and he is one of the most likely prominent types to actually secure his position.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins culminate in a career-best Temple Stakes Group 2 success at Haydock last time out, and with conditions and trip squarely in favour, Night Raider arrives in fine trim just 24 days later — the main risk is whether the bold front-running style holds up at this level.

runners_data.name: Overpass
runners_data.note: Australian raider from Bjorn Baker who goes well on good ground and places consistently at 6f; steps down to 5f for the first time in this campaign and that trip shortening is a genuine query, though he handles good ground well.
runners_data.comment: Consistent G1 performer whose T J Smith Stakes fourth (beaten 2l) sets the standard here, and dropping in trip to a stiff track plays to his strengths; yet to win in recent starts but rates clear top on our figures and will be tough to peg back.

runners_data.name: Rumstar
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's six-year-old was placed over 5f on good recently; a consistent prominent type who races without headgear and is reliable, though not flashy, and faces stiff competition from classier rivals.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a close second in a Group 3 on fast ground latest, and suits today's trip and conditions well; yet to score in recent starts and faces a stiff ask at this level after being outclassed here last year, but is clearly in better shape now.

runners_data.name: Shagraan
runners_data.note: Clive Cox-trained five-year-old with three wins at 5f including on good ground; an instinctively prominent runner who will find it hard to express that style in a field this size, and the redistribution to midfield is a real disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite last time in the Temple Stakes but holds Listed-class form over this trip and going — a multiple winner at this level who retains claims stepping back from Group company, though that Haydock flop leaves a question mark hanging over current form.

runners_data.name: Starlust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's horse has a win at 5f on firm going but his recent good-ground form shows several mid-field finishes; Rossa Ryan takes the ride and he appears a genuine prominent type whose 5f record on faster ground is limited.
runners_data.comment: Showed Group 1 class and ran encouragingly in this race last year, but winless in recent starts and must prove that sharpness is back after a stud sabbatical; the Carlisle Listed run 17 days ago should strip fitness forward.

runners_data.name: Asfoora
runners_data.note: Henry Dwyer's Australian mare heads into this race off two consecutive zeros having won at 5f on heavy and good ground; the headgear combination of tongue-tie and blinkers is retained, but her form suggests she may have peaked for now.
runners_data.comment: Defends her 2024 crown here, but two unplaced efforts this term — including a poor showing on easy ground at Haydock last time — raise questions about current form; the tongue-tie is new, fast ground suits, and a bounce-back from this proven G1 winner can't be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Azure Angel
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's six-year-old mare won at 5f on standard ground and is equipped with tongue-tie; an instinctively forward-going sort who is likely to find herself shuffled back in the pack and whose good-ground best form at this trip is limited.
runners_data.comment: Azure Angel steps up sharply in class after a creditable Listed effort last time, but at 130 lb from stall 25 and ranked 24 of 26 on our figures, the step into this grade looks a tough ask — first-time blinkers are a plus, though.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this four-year-old who won at 5f on soft ground, ridden by Cieren Fallon; a naturally up-with-the-pace runner who will need luck in running having been mapped back from her true position in a congested field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a G3 success in recent starts but has disappointed twice since, including a 6½-length beating last time out 45 days ago; acts on today's going and distance, yet improvement is needed if that winning form is to resurface.

runners_data.name: Frost At Dawn
runners_data.note: William Buick picks up the ride on this William Knight horse who wears a visor; has placed over 5f on good ground but his best recent finishes have come on softer surfaces, and being shuffled back from his natural prominent position is a disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and below-par at Haydock last time on easy ground, Frost At Dawn has the course-and-distance form and wears first-time cheekpieces that may spark a revival, though a disappointing 2025 campaign so far leaves plenty to prove from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's mare has shown only two runs on good going in the past 15 races, raising a clear concern on this surface; an instinctively prominent racer whose going record is a significant flag for this contest.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 2¼ lengths when second at York latest, Heavenly Heather has been progressive, but ranked last of 26 on our figures and drawn in stall 22, this looks a big ask at the weights.

runners_data.name: Mgheera
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's six-year-old has yet to win or place convincingly on good-to-firm going in 15 tries, which is a major concern on today's fast surface; a natural prominent type forced to midfield in a competitive field he may lack the pace to handle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and ranked well down our figures in a competitive field, Mgheera does at least have course-and-distance form on today's going and shaped with credit when beaten two lengths in a Group 2 last time, hinting at residual class.

runners_data.name: Miss Attitude
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Jack Channon who wears a tongue-piece and hood; her one 5f win came on good ground and she is a genuine come-from-behind type, but needs the pace to collapse in a field this size to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths in a Group 3 last time after missing the break, Miss Attitude's recent form reads consistently enough but she needs more to be competitive at this level, and ranked near the foot of our assessments, first-time cheekpieces must do the heavy lifting from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Monteille
runners_data.note: Mario Baratti's Italian-trained five-year-old has no wins or places on good going in 15 career efforts, which is an extremely worrying pattern; his hold-up style means he's relying on the race to come to him, which is doubly problematic.
runners_data.comment: Consistent Group winner in France who ran creditably when beaten two lengths in a Group 1 last time out, but fast ground remains a concern and the 80-day absence gives pause — capable of mixing it, though conditions may again blunt the edge.

runners_data.name: Rayevka
runners_data.note: French raider from Graffard who recorded a recent win over 5f on soft ground; a prominent racer whose only good-going win was at 5f in France, and being forced to race from midfield would represent a significant departure from her preferred conditions.
runners_data.comment: Rayevka arrives in form after a convincing Group 3 win at Longchamp 37 days ago, benefitting from a drop in trip and grade, and ran well at this very meeting last year — stiff 5f on today's going looks ideal, though 130lb and a field of 26 pose stiff tasks.

runners_data.name: Rosy Affair
runners_data.note: George Boughey's mare has won over 6f three times but steps down to a trip at which she has only one start — a fourth; mapped to hold-up because the field is over-stocked with prominent types, but she is not a natural closer and the trip is a query.
runners_data.comment: Rosy Affair arrives on the back of a Listed win at Haydock 25 days ago and has won three of her last five starts, but stepping up in class looks the key question for this progressive mare, who handles today's trip and conditions well enough.

runners_data.name: Time For Sandals
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old has a win at 6f on good ground but all five recent runs have come at 6f or further; the step down to a sharp 5f is a genuine concern and his wide-drawn tendencies may not suit a race this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Landed the Commonwealth Cup at this very meeting 12 months ago, so course form reads perfectly, and a trainer firing on all cylinders adds to the appeal after a first-run reappearance at York that arguably underflattered — there should be more to come. The wide draw from stall 9 is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Aspect Island
runners_data.note: James Owen's three-year-old wears a visor and has placed three times at 5f on good-to-firm ground; a naturally prominent racer unlikely to get his preferred position in this 26-runner field and lacks the experience of older rivals.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sprinter who ran a game race when a close third in Listed company last time out, but has been placed at the highest level and this demands even more again; the first-time visor is an interesting move, though, and 117 on our ratings suggests there's ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Behike
runners_data.note: George Scott's lightly-raced three-year-old won twice at 6f but steps sharply into Grade 1 company at 5f; limited form on good ground and David Egan has to overcome the inexperience and the scramble for position that a 26-runner sprint creates.
runners_data.comment: Boasts back-to-back wins including a cosy novice success at Lingfield last time, but steps up sharply in grade now and, ranked 20th of 26 in the field, this looks a big ask so early in its career.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien and Ryan Moore team up with a three-year-old who has won five of eight starts including back-to-back 5f wins on good ground; the combination of high-class trainer, top jockey, and strong recent 5f form on this surface makes him one of the most naturally suited prominent types in the race.
runners_data.comment: Confirmed the improvement shown as a two-year-old by winning a Listed sprint at Naas last time out, and still progressing with a top course jockey aboard; the step back to five furlongs from stall 24 on 127 lb may test, as connections likely prefer six.

races.paceDynamic: Big Mojo is the confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, is the only genuine lead horse in a 26-runner field packed with prominent-racing types — he will bowl along in front on Good To Firm ground at Ascot's straight 5f, setting a genuine but controlled tempo with little or no pressure from a true challenger for the lead. The field contains far more front-running and prominent types than can physically get their preferred position: Rayevka, Jm Jungle, Jakajaro, Getreadytorumble, Shagraan, Frost At Dawn, First Instinct, Azure Angel and others all want to race prominently but most will be shuffled back into midfield against their instincts in a 26-runner cavalry charge. With Big Mojo alone dictating from the front at a sustainable gallop, those racing in their natural position just off the pace — particularly American Affair, Night Raider, Cover Up, and Mission Central — are ideally placed to time their run, whereas horses redistributed to midfield or further back face the double disadvantage of racing out of role and needing the race to come back to them on a track that favours prominent racehorses. This race shape strongly favours horses who can genuinely secure a position in the first half-dozen — a sustainable pace with a lone leader rewards true prominent racers and horses with a high cruising speed rather than late closers.

watchPoints.text: Big Mojo leads uncontested but watch his sectional times at halfway — if he has opened up a clear advantage by the 2f pole, closing horses will have too much to do and prominent types behind him are the only realistic dangers.

The 26-runner draw is critical: watch for horses drawn wide on the far side who may be detached from the main action, as the straight Ascot 5f can produce split fields that leave runners on one flank racing in a separate race.

Rayevka, Jm Jungle and Jakajaro are all genuine prominent types who could not get their preferred positions — watch for any of them switching off and settling unexpectedly in the early stages, as that may indicate jockeys adapting to the race shape rather than fighting the crowd.

Mission Central's trainer-jockey combination (O'Brien/Moore) is notable in a race where securing a prominent position early is key — watch Moore's draw and early move to assess whether he can travel just behind Big Mojo on the rail or is forced wide.

Heavenly Heather and Mgheera both carry significant going concerns given their poor records on good ground — if the ground rides quick as the going report suggests, watch for both being beaten before the final furlong and use that as a pace-reading reference point mid-race.

races.name: St James's Palace Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)

runners_data.name: Bow Echo
runners_data.note: Four consecutive wins at a mile on Good ground is outstanding form for this track and trip; Billy Loughnane and George Boughey have him arriving fresh off 45 days and he is the only confirmed front-runner in the field — his chance hinges on whether he can control tempo with five prominent rivals pressing behind him.
runners_data.comment: Four wins on the spin culminate in a dominant 3-length 2000 Guineas success, where Bow Echo travelled supremely and quickened clear — a performance that marks him as the one to beat here, with proven course-and-distance form and 45 days to recover in good order.

runners_data.name: Gstaad
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore for Aidan O'Brien with seven winners from 31 runners in the last 14 days is a formidable combination; seven of eight runs on Good or similar ground with three wins tells a consistent story at this trip, and he has the natural prominent style and Group-class form to be first to challenge Bow Echo.
runners_data.comment: Bolted up in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time, quickening smartly to win by three lengths and advertise top-class mile form; proven on today's going and distance, with a top course jockey aboard from stall 1, though reversing Newmarket form remains the chief task.

runners_data.name: Lord Britain
runners_data.note: Arrives at OR 88 well below the class of his rivals and his recent form reading 38-401 contains a distant last at Group level; a true prominent racer who will struggle to assert his natural position in this field, and his two runs on comparable going produced no wins or placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Lord Britain won a handicap at Kempton last time on the all-weather, but is yet to prove effectiveness on turf and looks out of depth here; the first-time headgear may help, but this trip and surface combination remains unproven and our figures rank him last of six.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Won over six furlongs on Good ground and holds nine runs on similar going with a solid placed record, but four of his last five efforts include defeats at 7f-8f suggesting stamina at this level is a question; a natural pace-setter who will find prominent berths taken before him.
runners_data.comment: Power Blue showed Group 1 credentials when fourth in the Irish 2,000 Guineas last time but faces a re-opposing rival it couldn't beat there, and ranked fifth of six on our figures, a repeat performance looks unlikely to be enough here.

runners_data.name: Puerto Rico
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's second string carries strong Heavy-ground form — three of his four wins came on Heavy or Yielding — making the Good to Firm conditions here a genuine concern; pushed to the rear of the map by the weight of prominent types but is genuinely a horse that likes to race handy, which compounds the positional difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Puerto Rico brings a fine recent profile with two G1 victories to its name and an upward curve through the backend of last season, and a closing fourth in the Poule d'Essai at Longchamp on its return suggests the spark remains — the key question is whether it can reproduce that form on quicker ground today.

runners_data.name: Talk Of New York
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick send out a horse with three wins in his last four, all at 7f-8f on Good ground, which is an excellent profile for this trip and surface; worn hood in the past, arrives 19 days since last run, and his high cruising speed makes him the most likely of the redistributed prominent types to actually secure a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in its last four starts, including a scintillating 5½-length Listed victory at Sandown last time out, mark Talk Of New York as a serious threat; a trainer in form and a step up to today's mile suiting ideally, though first-time headgear adds a small unknown at this higher level.

races.paceDynamic: Bow Echo is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners and no genuine pace rival to push him, he should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground at Ascot's straight mile. The five remaining runners are all natural prominent types — Gstaad, Talk Of New York, Power Blue, Puerto Rico, and Lord Britain — meaning the positions directly behind Bow Echo will be fiercely contested from the outset, with several forced wider or further back than ideal. That compressed, pace-on-pace dynamic behind the leader is likely to produce a race that flows evenly from the front rather than building through gears, which classically rewards a horse that can travel smoothly in Bow Echo's slipstream and pick off a tiring leader in the final furlong. This shape strongly favours a genuine prominent-to-midfield traveller with a high cruising speed — specifically Gstaad, who has the class, the Aidan O'Brien/Ryan Moore combination, and the consistent Good-ground form to exploit a well-judged pace from just off the leader.

watchPoints.text: Bow Echo's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the pivotal factor — watch for Talk Of New York or Gstaad pressing forward early to test whether his lead can be sustained into the final furlong.
Puerto Rico's best form has come on Heavy ground and Good to Firm represents his quickest surface at Group 1 level — monitor his odds movement as going confirmation may prompt market reaction.

With five prominent-style horses chasing Bow Echo, a fierce battle for early position could develop in the opening two furlongs and cause physical interference — watch the draw and early stride patterns at the start.

Lord Britain's OR of 88 is 30+ pounds below the top three in the market; his presence is unlikely to shape the race tactically but his jockey Benoit De La Sayette may look to exploit any gaps created by the pace congestion ahead of him.

races.name: Ascot Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, Ian Williams' 6yo can control tempo entirely on his own terms at 2m4f on Good to Firm — was placed at Ascot in similar conditions and 11 days' freshness is a positive, though racing prominently is out of his deepest profile and a strong finishing field will likely reel him in.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but shaped with plenty of promise before flopping over a sharp trip last time; back up in distance today suits ideally, acts on this going, and first-time headgear could sharpen focus — though the trainer's current form gives pause.

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins hold-up type who was placed in this race twelve months ago; 248 days off is a significant concern for a horse who lacks a recent prep run, but Harry Vigors claiming 7lbs is a meaningful weight pull if fitness is there.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last four starts and found little when comfortably held last time, Bunting's best form has come over staying trips on the Flat, though it looks stable second string here and inconsistency over hurdles remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Barnso
runners_data.note: Alan King's 5yo is a prominent racer, 248 days since last run and a finishing position of 18th on his most recent start over this course and distance in similar going is very difficult to overlook as a negative.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with a string of fourths before a below-par latest effort, Barnso is winless in its last five but the step up to 14f-plus looks key — stamina questions loom on reappearance after 248 days off, however.

runners_data.name: Reaching High
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore booked for the second Mullins runner is always noteworthy, but 364 days off is a huge absence and his best recent form has come at shorter trips — the combination of lay-off and step up in trip requires confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Unlucky not to have won this 12 months ago when never getting a clear run and eased down beaten four lengths off the same mark, Reaching High lines up off an unchanged rating with course form and a top jockey aboard — the layoff is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners a genuine hold-up performer whose sole win came over 21f in soft, but he placed in this race at Ascot over 2m over Good in his most recent British start; the visor is retained and 60 days since last run is ideal freshness.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below par in recent outings, Lavender Hill Mob faces a stiff mark at 94, though the first-time visor and effectiveness across any going are mild positives worth monitoring after a 60-day break.

runners_data.name: Mordor
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes over on the Gordon Elliott raider who has won at 14f on good and placed over 24f — the strong recent form line of 1020-1 and proven Ascot form over 24f on Good is a compelling combination; prominent style suits this pace shape.|
runners_data.comment: Scored off a 7lb lower mark three starts back but was outstayed stepped up in trip last time; drops a significant 30lb here on a sound surface that suits, and proven course-and-distance form gives it every chance despite the inconsistent recent profile.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners a JP O'Brien runner who has shown solid form at up to 20f, including two placings at Group/Listed level; natural prominent style and 39 days since last run both sit comfortably for this test.|
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a close fourth at Chester last time off a 1lb lower mark, and this unexposed stayer's fine recent profile — including a runner-up effort — plus a significant jockey booking make her a leading danger, though she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted for this 7yo JP O'Brien runner whose form figures of 003-0P are deeply uninspiring and include a pulled-up run — headgear change is notable but the form demands a significant bounce-back.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up at Cork latest when the ground proved too testing, Comfort Zone is only 1lb higher than when placing in this race last year, giving it a clear angle — though below-par form this term is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Siempre Arturo
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer at 12f but this 2m4f trip represents a significant step up in distance for a horse whose five career runs have all been at 12f or under — trip doubt is the overriding concern.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces and a 38-day break since a run that needed, Siempre Arturo has the versatility across trips and surfaces to be competitive, but patchy recent form and the step up in trip still required leave this one looking a place player at best.

runners_data.name: Defiantly
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners the 4yo JP O'Brien filly who won at 12f in soft and has placed at 14f — the trip looks a stretch for a hold-up type whose best has been at shorter, and blinkers were fitted when pulled up last time out.|
runners_data.comment: Blinkers go on for the first time and there's a distance uptick that could suit this lightly-raced stayer, but inconsistent recent form and a lowly ranking on our figures make it hard to fancy with confidence.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin rides the lightly-raced 4yo who won impressively at Goodwood over 16f on Good last month; natural prominent profile and progressive form make him interesting if he can get his preferred position in a contested midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Bahadur lands in the crosshairs here after a willing 1¼-length Goodwood handicap success last time out, and this hugely progressive stayer looks the type with more to give over this trip — the main risk being a 4lb higher mark than when scoring.

runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy returns to the saddle for this JP O'Brien 5yo after 228 days off — a natural front-running type who will find himself unable to dictate as planned, forced back into an unfamiliar rear-of-midfield role that blunts his chances significantly.|

runners_data.name: Glenroyal

runners_data.name: Puturhandstogether
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on this JP O'Brien 5yo who naturally races prominently; unable to secure his preferred position in this 20-runner field, he is mapped to midfield but his best form has come when he has been allowed to stride on, making the redistribution damaging.|
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces on for the first time may sharpen this Fred Winter and Irish Cesarewitch winner, who remains relatively unexposed over staying trips, but last time out saw a well-beaten seventh at Chester and our figures have it well down the rankings here.

runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's 6yo is a confirmed prominent type who won over 16f on Good but has been off the track for a staggering 756 days — any fitness query after such a lengthy absence makes assessing his chance near impossible, and he too will be unable to secure a prominent berth with so many rivals ahead of him in the pecking order.|

runners_data.name: Annabel's Ghost
runners_data.note: Pierre-Charles Boudot takes the ride on this French-trained 5yo for M. Seror who won at 16f on Tapeta — a true hold-up performer mapped toward midfield; his form is best on soft or artificial surfaces and the Good to Firm conditions are an unknown quantity.|
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent French handicapper who plugged on for third on her penultimate outing but never threatened when beaten nine lengths at Longchamp last time; the step back to two miles and any cut in the ground help her cause, though her patchy record makes her hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Tim Toe
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 5yo arrives on the back of a Listowel Listed win over 12f just 16 days ago in fine form — but he is a natural prominent type who will be unable to get his favoured front-running position in this field, and the jump from 12f to 2m4f is extreme.|
runners_data.comment: Tim Toe arrives on the back of two wins in his last three starts, most recently edging a Listowel Conditions Race at the minimum of his stamina range — that trip drop a key form pointer. The mark looks lenient and a yard that won this last year gives confidence, though whether stamina holds at this distance is the crux.

runners_data.name: Kizlyar
runners_data.note: The JP O'Brien 4yo is a natural prominent racer who won last time over 14f on Good — recent form and going suit, but with the field overloaded with prominent types he is unlikely to get anywhere near his favoured position, blunting the impact of what looks solid in-form credentials.|
runners_data.comment: Kizlyar bounced back to win at Killarney last time out but sits at the foot of our rankings and looks to need plenty here; the ex-French gelding is lightly raced over marathon trips and a potentially lenient mark offers the sole grounds for optimism, with first-time headgear adding a wildcard.

races.paceDynamic: Beylerbeyi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field over 2m4f on Good to Firm ground at Ascot, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Billy Loughnane can control tempo from the front entirely on his own terms — setting a sustainable, measured gallop that plays directly into the hands of prominent and mid-division types who can travel close to the pace without expending energy early. The field contains a significant surplus of runners who naturally want to race prominently — Kizlyar, Small Fry, Puturhandstogether, Tim Toe and All In You among them — but with Beylerbeyi dictating, they cannot all secure their preferred position and will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield slots, compressing the pack and reducing the advantage of their natural style. With one horse controlling a steady gallop in a big, flat-course staying handicap, the race is unlikely to truly spring to life until well into the straight, meaning stamina reserves and the ability to quicken from a handy position will be paramount. This race shape strongly favours confirmed hold-up and genuine midfield stalkers who travel smoothly through the race and have a sustained late run, rather than those who need to use their engine early to secure position.

watchPoints.text: Beylerbeyi sets the entire race tempo alone — if Billy Loughnane produces a deceptively slow early gallop, watch for the field sitting motionless in a bunch until the straight, which could allow him to steal an advantage that is never recovered.|

Small Fry, Puturhandstogether, Kizlyar and Tim Toe are all confirmed prominent types who cannot all get their position — early jostling from these runners in the first half-mile could cause interference and hamper rivals racing in the lower draw positions.|

All In You has been absent for over two years; Edward Greatrex riding for his father's yard is a family booking but stable freshness after 756 days should be treated as a wild card — any market move would be significant.|

Mordor and Galileo Dame are the two prominent-profile runners with the clearest recent form and Ascot/distance credentials — their behaviour in the early stages as they settle behind the leader will largely dictate whether they have enough left to produce a late challenge.|

Bunting and Reaching High both arrive for Willie Mullins after very long absences (248 and 364 days respectively) — the stable's ability to produce horses fit first time back is well-documented, but neither has had a prep run and both are high-risk propositions on fitness grounds alone.|

races.name: Wolferton Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Adelaide River
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at Listed level for O'Brien but has been operating over 10-12f on good ground — the redistribution reflects a genuinely crowded prominent section, and he may find himself further back than his 1W4P prominent form demands; a 43-day absence adds minor freshness doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Adelaide River faces a stiff ask here, though first-time headgear and a return to his best trip could help — he's back in Ireland needing to prove he retains the level that once made him a Group winner.

runners_data.name: Ancient Wisdom
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old arrives on a 181-day break which is the key query, but his form shows a consistent pattern of placing over 10-12f and his two wins on good ground suggest the surface is fine; he holds a natural prominent position here and that is his biggest tactical asset in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Cheekpieces applied for the first time and a trainer in cracking form give Ancient Wisdom every chance on this surface, with proven course-and-distance form working in its favour — though the going remains the key concern for this winless-in-recent-starts performer, who was below-par on her latest All-Weather outing.

runners_data.name: Arabian Light
runners_data.note: Won last time over 10f on good ground for Appleby/Buick which is an obvious angle, but this field is too prominent-heavy for him to get his natural forward berth and he risks racing out of character in a midfield role he has rarely occupied; his 3W7P stat on similar ground underlines ability, but shape access is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when fourth at Sandown 19 days ago on a sound surface, and today's trip and conditions suit; a consistent Group 3 performer with a trainer in form, though ranked 10th of 16 here and likely needs improvement to land the spoils.

runners_data.name: Dividend
runners_data.note: Dr Newland and Insole's four-year-old has a sharp record of front-running wins (two in last five on good) but this is the horse most likely to crowd Ghostwriter's space — if he cannot get across, his style-fit suffers markedly in a non-prominent role; a well-related OR of 111 on a going profile of 10/15 is genuine raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just four lengths in a Group 1 in Dubai last time out gives Dividend some credibility, and it acts on today's going, but an 80-day break, first-time headgear, and a ranking of 15th of 16 on our figures make it very hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Enfjaar
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's six-year-old has not won in five runs (0W4P on similar going) and arrives off a 25-day break; he wants to be prominent but this race has no room for him at the front, and a horse with a history of grading through handicaps without winning looks vulnerable here in listed company out of role.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer whose good Goodwood Listed third on reappearance leaves him with improvement to come, and the yard has a strong record in this race — though winless in his last four starts remains the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Galen
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up horse has excellent course fitness — 14/15 runs on good ground — and the 122-day break is the only concern; he is one of the genuine hold-up types in the race (not a redistributed prominent) and his profile suits a scenario where the front-runners wilt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts yet a Group winner with a solid second in this race last year, Galen has clear course-and-distance credentials on a sound surface; however, the 122-day break and a thumping in Grade/Group company last time raise questions, even if first-time headgear could sharpen matters.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' seven-year-old has been racing on Flat/AW in Ireland (wins on standard ground, not good) and the going here is markedly faster than anything in his recent record; his form shows a prominent pattern but he is pushed back, making his challenge heavily dependent on conditions he is not proven on.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Gaucher faces a stiff task off 131 lb from stall 12, and 74 days off gives pause — though first-time headgear, a top jockey back aboard, and two wins in its last four starts for a powerful Irish yard offer crumbs of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ghostwriter
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's five-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and the race's pivotal shape-setter — a 360-day absence is a significant fitness concern, but if he is forward enough to stride to the front and settle, he controls the tactical picture entirely; David Egan's booking is purposeful.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with plenty of credit when a close third in a Group 2 last time out, and this represents a markedly easier task for a proven top-level performer who acts on today's ground and distance — the sole concern is whether 360 days off the track leaves him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Haatem
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old won over 10f on good ground and has three wins on similar going — he arrives 25 days fresh and James Doyle gives him a significant pilot upgrade; he is a natural prominent runner who can hold his position in this field, making him one of the better-placed horses if the race runs to the dominant shape.
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year and shaped with promise on his comeback at Goodwood 25 days ago, beaten three lengths in Listed company — that run under his belt should sharpen him up, though his last two efforts before that give reason for caution.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes the mount for Harry Charlton, which always implies a patient tactical ride, but this horse's form (1W6P on good ground) and recent finish of 9th suggests he is below the required level; though his style has been redistributed to midfield, he is unlikely to make the frame from any position in listed grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and below form when beaten eight lengths last time, King's Gambit nonetheless has placed twice in recent runs and acts on any going over today's trip — though connections may need to deploy him earlier than last year to turn placed efforts into something more.

runners_data.name: Map Of Stars
runners_data.note: French raider from Graffard with James McDonald — his good-ground form (3/12 records on similar) is limited, and his two recent runs have been 5th and 3rd on heavy/soft; the step up to good to firm here is a genuine concern and warrants caution despite his mid-range OR of 113.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and comfortably held in a Group 3 last time, Map Of Stars looks a stiff ask from stall 10 carrying 131 lb, ranked bottom of these on our figures. First-time cheekpieces and a useful run at this meeting last year offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Nahraan
runners_data.note: Gosden's lightly-raced four-year-old has won twice at Listed/Group level (1113 form) and Oisin Murphy is a high-profile booking — a 275-day layoff is the elephant in the room, and while his form profile is excellent, he is being asked to come back off a long break into a competitive listed race and his natural prominent style is now compromised by the crowded front section.
runners_data.comment: Nahraan showed smart form when winning three of his last four starts, but returns from a 275-day absence to tackle what looks a stiff ask, and despite a trainer firing at 29%, this comeback run may come too soon for a colt still with plenty of improvement ahead.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Sean Levey rides for Richard Hannon, and Persica has been racing over shorter (8-9f) mostly on soft — stepping up in trip to 10f on a faster surface is an untested combination; she is a genuine hold-up type and the 11-day turnaround is fine, but the style-going-trip combination needs examination before confidence.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhyme
runners_data.note: KR Burke's six-year-old has no wins from five runs on good ground (0W0P) and has been finishing in the 3-6 range over 10f on similar going — the form profile is consistent but below winning class, and without a significant career-best he looks a place-only proposition at best.
runners_data.comment: Royal Rhyme shaped with plenty of encouragement when finishing well after being caught too far back in a Group 2 last time, and a former Group winner returning to form with strong course claims, today's first-time headgear could be the spark that sees this winless-of-late performer finally deliver.

runners_data.name: Wimbledon Hawkeye
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon rides for James Owen, and this four-year-old has a solid record of placing over 10-12f on good to firm (0W6P, including two seconds); he is a natural prominent runner who can hold his position here, and his consistent placed form on quick ground makes him a core beneficiary of the dominant pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths on return at Sandown last time but shaped as though that run will have sharpened him up, and he's a likeable Group 2/3 performer effective over this trip on any going; the first-time cheekpieces add an interesting angle, though 131 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Survie
runners_data.note: George Boughey's five-year-old carries a 3lb allowance (126lbs) which is a material weight concession in a level-weights contest, and Ryan Moore's booking is notable; however, he has no wins on good going and his redistributed midfield placement puts him in an unnatural position — his best form came on easier ground and at different trips.
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Group 2 on her latest start 44 days ago, Survie has course-and-distance form and a top jockey aboard, while first-time headgear could sharpen her up — though she ideally wants cut in the ground, which is the key concern on today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Ghostwriter is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, critically, is unlikely to face serious pressure for the lead — he can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Ascot. The field is saturated with prominent-running types: Survie, Dividend, Arabian Light, Enfjaar, Nahraan, Gaucher, King's Gambit and Adelaide River all want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy that ground, meaning several will be shuffled back into unnatural midfield positions and effectively race out of their preferred role. With Ghostwriter controlling the tempo unchallenged, the pace will be steady to moderate in the early stages, likely quickening from the home turn rather than punishing the field with sustained front-running fractions — this is a classic setup for a well-positioned sit-and-sprint race shape. The tactical verdict is clear: horses that can travel prominently or just off a single uncontested front-runner — particularly those with a sharp turn-of-foot on good ground — are best placed, while genuine hold-up horses relying on a true end-to-end gallop to generate their finishing run will find the race shape against them.
