watchPoints.text: Ghostwriter's 360-day absence is the single biggest race-shape risk — if he is not fit enough to sustain his lead after the home turn, the entire dominant scenario collapses and the race opens up dramatically for hold-up horses.

Ancient Wisdom returns from 181 days off for Appleby — Charlie Appleby's horses returning from long breaks at Royal Ascot have a strong record, but if he is underdone the prominent sector loses its most credible pace-shape winner.

Nahraan's 275-day layoff combined with a prominent runner's natural position being crowded out means Oisin Murphy must make a critical decision at the start — any hesitation forces him into a midfield role his form profile does not suit.

The sheer volume of prominent-type runners (eight-plus) risks producing a chaotic early scrimmage for position despite only one confirmed front-runner — watch for a fractious first two furlongs as Dividend, Haatem and Arabian Light all contest the same ground behind Ghostwriter.

Map Of Stars' going record on genuinely fast ground is thin (3/12 on similar), and James McDonald may elect to produce him late from midfield — if the pace does collapse late, he is the dark horse whose French form may be underestimated by UK punters.

races.name: Copper Horse Stakes (Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground and has course-and-distance experience, making the trip a clear strong suit; travels prominently and will be comfortable if he gets a position just behind the front rank, though a 46-day break and moderate recent form at OR 100 give reason to temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Won off a 5lb lower mark on this card last year and effective over marathon trips on any ground, but Ascending may have reached a plateau and was well beaten in a Group 3 latest, suggesting the current mark is against it.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will set the pace unchallenged; has a STYLE_FIT flag for racing out of his normal role context here, but the position itself is natural — the concern is whether his best form is at 12f not 14f, and his recent 7th and 2nd at shorter trips suggests fitness but possible trip doubt.
runners_data.comment: Consistent prior to a puzzling below-par York flop latest, Stressfree ticks the boxes on distance and going and rates a leading danger on our figures — the main risk is whether that York run left its mark.

runners_data.name: Paddy The Squire
runners_data.note: Three wins and six places on good ground in the last year make the going no concern; a natural front-rank type who will be pressing to get a prominent slot, and the tongue-piece suggests a keenness management angle — if he secures cover just off Stressfree, his big-field Ascot trip record reads well.
runners_data.comment: Runners-up twice and a dual winner in recent starts, Paddy The Squire has course-distance-going form to draw on, but two disappointing efforts since those wins — including being outpaced and beaten over eight lengths at York — suggest the current mark may have caught up with him, and first-time cheekpieces plus a cold trainer compound the concern.

runners_data.name: Daiquiri Bay
runners_data.note: Bounced back to win last time on good ground over 12f and is going the right way as a lightly-raced four-year-old; a prominent runner who should slot in comfortably third or fourth given the redistribution squeeze elsewhere, and Rossa Ryan is experienced in pacing these staying handicaps.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who won a Boodles Handicap at Newmarket last time off a 4lb lower mark, but now racing off a revised rating that raises the bar; acts on today's conditions and distance, though the higher weight and mark are legitimate questions.

runners_data.name: Hallelujah U
runners_data.note: Has been off 318 days (213 days jumps-side), which is the most significant flag in the field — a winning return at OR 100 in a 16-runner Ascot handicap would be a big ask; wears a hood and has a prominent style, but the layoff overshadows everything else here.
runners_data.comment: Proven over course and distance, the first-time cheekpieces could sharpen this strong-staying type who acts on today's conditions, and the yard has a good record with similar profiles — though a disappointing latest run and an absence since leaves fitness the main query.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form reads 7-7-13-4-6, giving little encouragement; the tongue-strap is noted and Ian Williams's yard is 0/42 in the 14-day window, making this a difficult horse to build a case around despite an adequate going profile.
runners_data.comment: Real Dream has been winless in its last five starts but arrives with the handicapper relenting and today's longer trip a clear plus on a sound surface it handles well; first-time headgear adds interest and our top rating of 119 marks this as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yashin
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who handles good ground and has placed three times in similar staying handicaps; Tom Marquand is an intelligent judge of pace and will likely ride cold from the back, but the 12th and 22nd in his last two competitive runs make his chance dependent on a very slow early gallop.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and well beaten in a Newmarket handicap on his most recent outing 44 days ago, Yashin looks flattered by last year's Group win on this course and has been too inconsistent to fancy under a big weight, despite a significant jockey booking and proven course-and-distance form.

runners_data.name: Gamrai
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden four-year-old who has won twice and placed three times in six starts on similar ground; Oisin Murphy is the standout booking in a race short of star jockeys and will likely sit prominently on a horse whose best form has come over shorter, though the step up to 1m6f is the key query.
runners_data.comment: Quickened well but probably hit the front too soon and was caught late when second off a mark of 97 last time — 2lb higher here and ranked well down our figures, Gamrai looks up against it despite the yard winning this race last year.

runners_data.name: Enemy
runners_data.note: Has won twice at Wolverhampton's 16f on standard going but has zero placed runs on turf in the last 15 outings; the trainer is cold at 0/42 over 14 days, the horse is nine years old, and his turf profile at this trip is unconvincing — stamina is there, turf effectiveness less so.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7¼ lengths at Carlisle last time when unsuited by the drop in trip, Enemy is better judged on earlier successes and remains on a competitive mark over today's distance and going — though a struggling trainer strike-rate and first-time headgear introduce some uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Valiancy
runners_data.note: Five wins and six places on good ground and is unbeaten in three starts at 1m1f-1m6f this season at OR 98; though William Haggas's horse is a true front-rank type who ideally wants to bowl along, he is mapped to midfield due to the overcrowded prominent positions — his exceptional recent form means he retains strong claims if James Doyle can find a position just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Boasts a fine recent sequence — three wins in its last five starts, including a cosy 1¼-length handicap success at Hamilton off a mark 8lb lower than today — and is a rapidly progressing stayer with more improvement expected; the 8lb rise and 136lb burden are the chief concerns for a trainer firing at 37%.

runners_data.name: Green Cape
runners_data.note: Won over 11f at Lingfield on soft and has a tongue-tie; returning from 129 days off and has only two placed runs from nine efforts on good or good-to-firm ground — the quick ground and fitness after the layoff are the twin concerns that overshadow what is a naturally forward-going horse squeezed into a midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Green Cape is last on our figures and has been inconsistent in recent starts, while 129 days off the track adds to the query marks; first-time cheekpieces and a switch of stable offer slim hope, but this looks a tough ask at the weights.

runners_data.name: Aeronautic
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's five-year-old has placed three times in five starts on good ground and is a consistent third-placed performer; naturally prominent, he arrives 116 days off the track and John Velazquez is an unusual booking — the combination of absence and not getting his natural position dampens his outlook.
runners_data.comment: Winless in its last five starts and comfortably held in a Group 3 last time out, Aeronautic holds few secrets from the handicapper and returns after a 116-day break; first-time headgear and proven course-and-distance form offer slim positives, but this looks a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Duraji
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good ground at Brighton and has sound each-way form in staying handicaps; held up by Finley Marsh, this horse is better suited to a genuinely run race and the 39-day break looks routine — a contender if the pace gets serious but left behind in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who shaped with promise at Chester last time, beaten a length off a 2lb lower mark, and a drop in trip looks a plus; winless in recent starts and a hefty 135lb may test its chances of converting.

runners_data.name: Sing Us A Song
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on soft and has placed twice on good ground, but his best efforts have come on easier surfaces; Ralph Beckett's string is in form at 9/44 over 14 days and McDonald is an elite booking — a natural prominent runner pushed into midfield, and on genuinely good ground, the surface might just be on the quick side of ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form when a game second at York last time off a 2lb lower mark, and there's reason to think longer distances will unlock more — effective at 12-14f and potentially better beyond, though today's trip and the 135lb burden are the key variables to weigh.

runners_data.name: Ernst Blofeld
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Wolverhampton on standard and has placed once in eight turf starts on good ground; the big drop in trip from his winning distance and the unproven turf form on this ground type mean he is largely speculative despite a recent 1st suggesting some return to form.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Kempton handicap off a 7lb lower mark last time, so the revised rating makes this considerably tougher, and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, it's hard to fancy despite proven ability on today's going over this trip.

runners_data.name: Incensed
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on good ground and twice on standard at 12f trips; a natural front-rack type nudged into a midfield berth due to the overcrowded prominent positions, and Amanda Perrett is 0/7 in the 14-day window — the combination of style displacement and a cold yard makes it hard to be enthusiastic.
runners_data.comment: Consistent filly who proved her Listed-class credentials with a close third at Goodwood 46 days ago, and she's proven effective over today's trip on this surface — the main worry is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Stressfree is the one confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field over 1m6f at Ascot on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Daniel Tudhope can dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front. That measured tempo will compress the race into a stamina-and-kick contest from the home turn rather than a true test of grinding endurance, making the final three furlongs the decisive phase. The field is overloaded with horses who want to race prominently — Valiancy, Green Cape, Aeronautic, Sing Us A Song, Incensed and Paddy The Squire all have front-rank tendencies but cannot all get their natural position, meaning several will be shuffled into an uncharacteristic midfield slot, diluting their effectiveness. This shape strongly favours horses who can settle comfortably off a steady pace and then produce a sharp turn of foot — prominent types who find a clean position just behind Stressfree, or hold-up horses with a genuine late gear, will be best placed, provided they have the class to quicken on good ground at Ascot.

watchPoints.text: Valiancy — William Haggas's unbeaten-this-season four-year-old is the most naturally talented horse in the field but will be forced to settle off the prominent position he prefers; watch how quickly James Doyle manoeuvres him into a tracking role, because if he gets cover and a clean run, his turn of foot on good ground is the biggest danger in the race.

Gamrai — Oisin Murphy on a Gosden four-year-old going the right way is always worth monitoring; the concern is whether 1m6f stretches his stamina past its limit given all five runs have been at shorter, and if the pace is slow his finishing kick may arrive too late or too close to the wire.

Hallelujah U — the 318-day absence (213 days on jumps) is the longest layoff in the field and must be flagged clearly; horses returning after that length of time into a competitive 16-runner Ascot handicap on good ground are statistically at a significant disadvantage, regardless of the promising profile on paper.

Stressfree — although he holds the leading position on the map, his STYLE_FIT note and recent form at shorter trips mean if he either goes too slow (sets up a sprint he cannot win) or is outpaced late, the race may play into the hands of the closers tracking him; the pace he elects to set will shape every other scenario.

Sing Us A Song — James McDonald's booking for Ralph Beckett (9/44 in 14 days) on a horse that is a true prominent type is worth watching at the off; if the gate opens and McDonald sends him forward to claim one of the limited front-rank slots rather than accepting midfield, the race shape could shift marginally toward the pace-setting group.
